findings.text: follow-on: the two sibling tests test_a_scoring_run_dispatches_its_own_review_unasked (:267) and test_an_unavailable_lane_is_recorded_and_a_returning_lane_dispatches (:296) keep the fragile teardown this node repaired in the target test - an immediate `if crew.watch_state("sample")["watcher_live"]: recovery.unwatch("sample")` - so they can read a seat registration mid-rewrite and hit the same `refusing to stop watcher for project 'sample': the locked registration names ''` the target test hit. They were green in compute-file.log, but the window is unclosed.

follow-on: unwatch decides a seat is foreign from the raw registration alone (`registered_project = str(watcher.get("project") or ""); if registered_project != project: raise`), so a live local producer whose registration is mid-write is momentarily un-unwatchable. watch_state reconciles the same record against the live holder before reporting (reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:203), so a caller cannot observe that transient there; unwatch could reconcile likewise instead of refusing on the record alone. The node repaired the test's teardown rather than the product, so the robustness gap stays open.
